_notes: Metallica Pro 1.80. Everything here was measured from a 1,600-frame recording of live memory
spanning an operator-menu session and a full four-player game with a tilt on player 1's ball 1,
then confirmed against the machine's own displays. The Premium map (mtl_180h) was tried first:
its score slots fit this ROM exactly, its ball/player pair does not (that address reads 0 here).
current_player/current_ball came from the joint pair test -- the player wrapping to 1 in the
same sample the ball steps -- which returned exactly one candidate across four such events.
Scores: 4 bytes on 8-byte centres from 0x02110A24, the same slots the Premium uses; finals for
all four players sat frozen from game over through attract.
Adjustments are 8-byte records from 0x02102008 (32-bit value, then 0xFF minus the sum of its
bytes); Balls Per Game and Maximum Credits identified by setting them to 5 and 9 (indices 32 and
34), free_play at index 35 read 0 with a valid check byte while credits were being consumed.
credits at 0x0211100C, the twelfth SAM game at that address: rose to 7 with the coins and fell
once for each of the four players entering.
0x00030B7A is the status bitfield most SAM games keep at ball+0x31, in a variant of its own: 1
in attract, 42 (0x2A) at each ball's start, 20 (0x14) in play, 22 (0x16) for exactly the seven
samples between the tilt and the end of the tilted ball, during which player 1's score sat
frozen at 265,530. No single bit separates play from attract, so game_over uses mask 0x30
(0x10 covers 20 and 22, 0x20 covers 42) inverted -- correct in all 1,600 frames. No single bit
separates the tilt either: 22 is 0x02 and 0x04 both set, while 42 carries 0x02 and 20 carries
0x04. tilted is therefore declared as alien_poker does it, an enum over mask 0x06 in which only
the value 6 is true.
Champion records are 36 bytes with initials at +0, score at +0x18 and a little-endian checksum16
at +32 over the first 32 bytes, all 15 validating. The five high scores come first. The ten mode
champions were named from the game-over display cycle. Eight of the ten are pinned by a unique
Lady Justice Champion is ABC 2,500,000 -- confirmed against the display on a second look; the
first reading of 7,500,000 was the DMD font.
The operator menu's champion settings do NOT write the records above. They write a default-
threshold table of 8-byte adjustment records at 0x021024F8, stride 0x18, nine modes in the order
Battery, Enter Sandman, Fade To Black, For Whom The Bell Tolls, Fuel, Lady Justice, Seek &
Destroy, The End Of The Line, Blackened (Combo, a count, is elsewhere). Setting Battery to
28,000,000 and Fade To Black to 26,000,000 changed exactly those slots and their check bytes and
left every record untouched; the records take the thresholds only on a champion reset. That
table is also why the record order cannot be assumed from mtl_170h: the thresholds follow
mtl_170h's order and the records do not (Blackened is record +2).
All ten mode champions are pinned. Eight by a unique initials/score pair from the game-over
display cycle; the two ABC 25,000,000 records (+1 and +4) were settled by setting distinct
thresholds -- Battery 28,000,000, Fade To Black 26,000,000, For Whom The Bell Tolls 27,000,000
-- and running the operator menu's champion reset: +1 took 28,000,000 and +4 took 26,000,000,
with +5 (MDK) taking 27,000,000. The reset applied the thresholds to the scores and left the
initials in place.

The record is 36 bytes with the checksum at +32, so four bytes sit between the 4-byte score at
+24 and the checksum. They read zero in every image captured (163 records across five games)
and their purpose is not established: they are consistent with the upper half of a 64-bit score,
but this game's champion-threshold table at 0x021024F8 stores its thresholds as 4-byte values
with a complement check byte, which is what a 32-bit score would be compared against. The score
is therefore declared as 4 bytes until a value above 2^32 is observed or the ROM is disassembled.
2026-11: Master Volume and the A.1 (64) and A.2 (131) adjustments added from the ROM image
(README, 'Adjustments from the ROM').
Confirmed on a cabinet 2026-11-13 (ALP4K; two players, tilt on P1 ball 1): 2,002,800 /
1,251,560, the records and the status byte (01, 2A ball served, 14 play, 16 tilted) matched the
DMD.
